4  JUDGMENT Vinod Chandran, J.
The petitioner, a private limited company, is said to have initiated a novel project of having a chain of department stores on the basis of franchisee agreements entered into with various persons in different localities.

entities.text: S.Janasevana Nyayavila Bazaar Pvt. ... vs The District Police Chief on 30 August, 2017 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The party respondents herein are said to be persons, who have entered into agreements with the petitioner.

The petitioner having taken a security deposit from the franchisees,
in proportion to the extent of the shop buildings offered by the franchisees, has carried out interior works and has also supplied materials for sale in the franchisee's unit.
The arrangement was that the sale price would be remitted to the petitioner company and the franchisees would be given a monthly remuneration.
The petitioner's contention is that the WP(C) 694/2018 franchisees themselves started selling their own products within the shops and failed to deposit the amounts due to the petitioner company.
Not only that the 12th respondent is said to have ransacked the petitioner's premises and taken away many goods.
The petitioner lodged a complaint as seen from Ext.P5 and also gave a representation to the District Police Chief apprehending that the other franchisees would repeat what the 12 th respondent did.
2. Respondents 5, 6, 8 and 11 do not appear.
Advocate Shri D.Kishore appearing for respondents 7, 9 and 10 specifically points out that there is no allegation against any of the party respondents, but the 12th respondent.
The Writ Petition has been filed merely on an apprehension.

It is also the submission of respondents 7, 9 and 10 that there has been serious misappropriation of funds by the petitioner on the basis of the so-called chain of super markets and that huge amounts were taken from the party respondents, who have filed complaints before the respective police stations.

It is also the specific WP(C) 694/2018 contention of the party respondents that the complaints together has to result in an investigation by the Special Branch CID as per Circular No.22/2013 as an economic offence, since the amounts involved exceed Rs.2 crores.
It is submitted that respondents 7, 9 and 10 have filed complaints and so would the others.
3. The 12th respondent categorically submits that there was no incident of a ransacking of the petitioner's premises.
In fact, the 12th respondent, dissatisfied with the franchisee agreement, had taken the goods supplied by the petitioner company back to his premises, which was refused.
These goods were taken back in two lorries on the basis of which a complaint was raised by the petitioner.

4. We find that essentially the disputes are contractual in nature and that there is absolutely no reason why this Court should decide on the legitimacy of the allegations of either of these parties in the present Writ Petition.

Suffice it to notice that both the parties have filed criminal complaints, in which action in accordance with law, will be taken by the Police, proper WP(C) 694/2018 investigation conducted and proceedings initiated against those charged of offences under the Indian Penal Code or under any other Statute.
The learned Counsel for the party respondents also submits that they do not propose to take law into their hands.
The said submission is recorded and the Writ Petition is rejected.
No costs.
